metadata.scenario: A prospect calls in to dispute a service charge they were not informed about. Category: Billing. Flags: billing_dispute.

transcription.text: Thank you for calling CareFirst Home Health, this is Margaret. How can I assist you today? Hi Margaret, this is Frank Miller. I've got an issue with a service charge on my recent billing statement. Hi Frank, I’m glad you called. Can you tell me more about the charge you’re disputing? Sure, I was charged for wound care on my last visit, but I wasn't informed about any additional fees. I understand your concern. Let me pull up your account and review the details. One moment please. Okay, take your time. Thank you for your patience, Frank. I see that there was an extra charge for a nurse's overtime due to an extended visit yesterday. It appears we didn’t communicate this properly. Well, I wasn't aware that was going to happen, and it seems unfair. I completely understand, and I apologize for the oversight. We strive for transparency in our billing. So, what can we do about this charge? I can initiate a review of this charge, and depending on the findings, we can issue a credit if it was an error. That sounds good. How long will that take? Typically, it takes 3-5 business days to complete the review. I’ll ensure you’re updated via email. Great, I appreciate that. Also, while I have you on the line, would you like to discuss your monthly transportation needs for your endocrinologist visits? Yes, that’d be helpful. I need a ride once a month. We offer transportation services for $45 to $65 per trip. Would you like to set that up? Yes, I’d like to go ahead and arrange that. Perfect! I’ll include that in our follow-up email, along with the billing update. Thank you, Margaret. I appreciate your help with this. You're welcome, Frank. Is there anything else I can assist you with today? No, that's everything for now. Okay, thank you for calling CareFirst. Have a great day! You too, bye! Bye!
